blocks.x: While Laurie Strode is an integral part of John Carpenter's original Halloween, Jamie Lee Curtis didn't reprise her iconic role in the franchise's latest adaptation. Instead, Laurie is officially voiced by Chelsea Krause in Halloween: The Game, which launched on September 8, 2026.

Krause, whose previous voice-acting credits include Genshin Impact and Dune: Awakening, takes over the role in developer IllFonic's adaptation of the 1978 horror classic. Interestingly, the game doesn't have the rights to Curtis' likeness, meaning Laurie's appearance has also been revamped while still being recognizable as the original film's heroine.

Despite those changes, Krause has gone to considerable lengths to recreate Curtis' memorable performance. In a September 6 social media post, the actress clarified that all of Laurie's dialogue, screams, and other vocal performances are entirely her own, revealing that nearly half her recording sessions involved matching scenes from the original movie.

Laurie as a character plays an important role in the game, appearing throughout the single-player campaign, which retells the events of the original film from Michael Myers' perspective. Players encounter Laurie alongside other familiar characters, including Annie Brackett, Lynda van der Klok, and Bob Simms. Laurie is actually a playable civilian in the game's asymmetrical multiplayer mode, where players must work together to survive Michael's murderous rampage, rescuing Haddonfield residents and hopefully escaping (if they're lucky).

Players can even unlock alternate outfits inspired by the original film by completing challenges throughout the single-player campaign, letting fans experience Laurie's iconic Halloween night in a fresh new way.

blocks.x: Aside from introducing a new actress as Laurie Strode, Halloween: The Game offers a fresh take on John Carpenter's original 1978 film. Developed by IllFonic, the game revisits Michael Myers' infamous killing spree in Haddonfield, allowing players to experience the events of that fateful Halloween night through the killer's eyes.

The single-player campaign, titled The Night He Came Home, follows Michael as he stalks his victims throughout Haddonfield, recreating recognizable moments from Carpenter's original masterpiece while giving players opportunities to approach events differently. Certain challenges even encourage players to follow the film's established storyline, offering an incentive if you remain faithful to the source material.

Unfortunately, Halloween: The Game has received a somewhat mixed reception since launching on September 8, 2026. Its Steam user reviews currently sit at a Mixed rating, with about just 68% positive feedback, with opinions largely divided. While the premise is a selling point and the story/gameplay seem to be fun, players have reported frustrating bugs, performance problems, and balance issues.

However, IllFonic has continued supporting the game through several post-launch updates and improvements addressing these issues. Most recently, Patch 1.1.0 arrived on October 6, introducing substantial crash fixes, performance optimizations, improved NPC behavior, and numerous gameplay adjustments. The developers have also announced additional content arriving October 27, including a free map inspired by Halloween 5 and new Michael Myers appearances based on the fifth film and the 2018 reboot.

For anyone interested in experiencing Michael's terrifying return to Haddonfield firsthand, Halloween: The Game is available now on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, and PC via Steam and the Epic Games Store.

While Laurie Strode is an integral part of John Carpenter's original Halloween, Jamie Lee Curtis didn't reprise her iconic role in the franchise's latest adaptation. Instead, Laurie is officially voiced by Chelsea Krause in Halloween: The Game, which launched on September 8, 2026.

Krause, whose previous voice-acting credits include Genshin Impact and Dune: Awakening, takes over the role in developer IllFonic's adaptation of the 1978 horror classic. Interestingly, the game doesn't have the rights to Curtis' likeness, meaning Laurie's appearance has also been revamped while still being recognizable as the original film's heroine.

Despite those changes, Krause has gone to considerable lengths to recreate Curtis' memorable performance. In a September 6 social media post, the actress clarified that all of Laurie's dialogue, screams, and other vocal performances are entirely her own, revealing that nearly half her recording sessions involved matching scenes from the original movie.

Laurie as a character plays an important role in the game, appearing throughout the single-player campaign, which retells the events of the original film from Michael Myers' perspective. Players encounter Laurie alongside other familiar characters, including Annie Brackett, Lynda van der Klok, and Bob Simms. Laurie is actually a playable civilian in the game's asymmetrical multiplayer mode, where players must work together to survive Michael's murderous rampage, rescuing Haddonfield residents and hopefully escaping (if they're lucky).

Players can even unlock alternate outfits inspired by the original film by completing challenges throughout the single-player campaign, letting fans experience Laurie's iconic Halloween night in a fresh new way.

Halloween Rewrites John Carpenter's Original Story

Aside from introducing a new actress as Laurie Strode, Halloween: The Game offers a fresh take on John Carpenter's original 1978 film. Developed by IllFonic, the game revisits Michael Myers' infamous killing spree in Haddonfield, allowing players to experience the events of that fateful Halloween night through the killer's eyes.

The single-player campaign, titled The Night He Came Home, follows Michael as he stalks his victims throughout Haddonfield, recreating recognizable moments from Carpenter's original masterpiece while giving players opportunities to approach events differently. Certain challenges even encourage players to follow the film's established storyline, offering an incentive if you remain faithful to the source material.

Unfortunately, Halloween: The Game has received a somewhat mixed reception since launching on September 8, 2026. Its Steam user reviews currently sit at a Mixed rating, with about just 68% positive feedback, with opinions largely divided. While the premise is a selling point and the story/gameplay seem to be fun, players have reported frustrating bugs, performance problems, and balance issues.

However, IllFonic has continued supporting the game through several post-launch updates and improvements addressing these issues. Most recently, Patch 1.1.0 arrived on October 6, introducing substantial crash fixes, performance optimizations, improved NPC behavior, and numerous gameplay adjustments. The developers have also announced additional content arriving October 27, including a free map inspired by Halloween 5 and new Michael Myers appearances based on the fifth film and the 2018 reboot.

For anyone interested in experiencing Michael's terrifying return to Haddonfield firsthand, Halloween: The Game is available now on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, and PC via Steam and the Epic Games Store.
